messages:
Mohit: Ran a 12h KV-cache long-run profiler across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. Pattern is a repeating ramp + partial drop (not full GC) every ~250s on Dedicated and Private; Hosted looks smoother but has micro-spikes near long-context tails. Putting top traces and a couple of dumps here.

Mohit: Dedicated jemalloc summary (sanitized):
```
allocated: 4.8G  active: 5.2G  resident: 5.3G
arenas: 8  dirty_pct: 22%  retained: 150M
muzzy_decay_ms: 600000  dirty_decay_ms: 300000
fragmentation_est: 9.3%
```

Mohit: Private (on-prem) shows similar resident growth but retained pages never shrink (madvise seems ineffective on our custom kernel). Hosted: allocated 4.7G resident 4.9G but retained drops periodically to 60MB.

Ana: kernel/cgroup diffs? cgroup v2 mem.high behavior can cause short reclaim bursts instead of full reclaim. Which kernels are we running across fleets?

Mohit: Hosted nodes = 6.4.x, Dedicated = 5.15.x (we kept some legacy images), Private = 5.10.x custom. cgroup v2 enabled everywhere but mem.high set only on Hosted. Dedicated/Private have zone_reclaim=1 for NUMA locality (legacy).

Jenna: Interesting. Our batching heuristic expands window when latency headroom is seen which spikes concurrent KV frame allocations. Those mid-size allocations live across request pipeline stages and increase fragmentation. Did you try forcing batch_size=1 or disable adaptive batching?

Mohit: Quick AB: Hosted w/ batch_size=1 -> sawtooth amplitude mostly gone. Dedicated w/ batch_size=1 -> amplitude reduced but still present. Private w/ batch_size=1 -> almost unchanged. So batching contributes but doesn't explain on-prem behavior.

Sam: On Dedicated we recently adjusted IRQ/CPU affinity and set numa_balancing off; that changed page placement (more cross-node pages). zone_reclaim=1 will try to keep pages local and can trigger slow reclaim loops. Try toggling zone_reclaim to 0 on a repro box.

Mohit: Did that on a repro machine: zone_reclaim=0 flattened the ramp slope significantly and reduced RSS growth rate.

Ana: On Private, our custom kernel short-circuits madvise MADV_DONTNEED for a range of VMAs to avoid compaction pauses for long-running drivers. That explains retained pages not returned to kernel --- jemalloc calls madvise but kernel ignores it.

Jenna: Two actionable quick tests: 1) set jemalloc decay tunables via MALLOC_CONF (e.g., dirty_decay_ms=300000,muzzy_decay_ms=600000) to force faster release; 2) add a periodic kv::trim() that calls madvise on cold frames every N requests. Which one did you try?

Mohit: I tried lowering decay to dirty_decay_ms=60k,muzzy_decay_ms=120k on Dedicated repro; resident dropped 70-120MB and sawtooth amplitude smaller. On Private it had almost no effect (kernel is ignoring madvise). Hosted responded well.

Sam: Also worth checking hugepage/THP settings. THP can make large allocations back heavier to reclaim and cause bumpy behaviour. Are we allocating any contiguous huge mappings for KV frames?

Mohit: We don't explicitly use hugetlbfs, but allocator sometimes maps large extents. THP is enabled on Private for legacy gpudriver reasons. Turning THP off in a guest reduced Private retained growth in one quick test.

Ana: cgroup v2 mem.swap.max and mem.high interplay: on Hosted we set mem.high threshold low which triggers proactive reclaim and keeps resident flatter. Dedicated had no mem.high set, so reclaim happens only when under pressure -> bigger ramps. Consider setting mem.high for Dedicated pools or tuning mem.high + swap.max.

Jenna: From runtime side: we can reduce per-request transient KV allocations by preallocating a small object pool (kv frame slab) and reusing frames across requests. That should lower mid-size allocation churn and fragmentation. Any perf downside?

Mohit: Implemented a quick pool prototype: reduced alloc churn by ~40% and lowered fragmentation metric in jemalloc stats. Combined with jemalloc decay tweaks, Hosted and Dedicated look much better. Private still stubborn due to kernel maddive/THP behavior.

Sam: For Private we may need an explicit compaction path inside the runtime: when growth rate > X over Y seconds, we call a background worker that walks cold KV frames and writes them to a compacted backing store (or spill to disk) then madvise/destroy the VMAs. Ugly but pragmatic for on-prem.

Ana: Also add a health metric: "kv_retained_bytes" + growth_rate alarm. If growth_rate > threshold AND kernel_madvise_ignored -> trigger spill/trim.

ci-bot: Perf artifacts uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/artifacts/2833333333/kv-longrun (profiles + jemalloc dumps + vmstat samples)

Jenna: Next steps: 1) Prod-like Dedicated: enable mem.high at a conservative level and test; 2) Hardening: KV frame pool + configurable jemalloc decay in runtime config; 3) Private: document kernel caveats (madvise/THP) for on-prem installs and add runtime fallback to spill/compact.

Mohit: I'll open a ticket with repro steps + attach artifact link and add a small patch to set MALLOC_CONF from the runtime config so we can iterate without rebuilds. Thanks team. :raised_hands:
